title: Personal Credit Cards: Deficit on an Overdrawn Autopay Checking Account
content:
Where Personal Credit Cards points are used to restore the checking account that pays a card by automatic payment, the size of the gap to be closed is the account's deficit, defined here.

## Definition

The deficit is read from the ledger balance of the checking account the card names as its autopay source, at the time the matter is handled. A ledger balance below zero gives a deficit equal to that negative figure stated as a positive sum. A ledger balance of zero or above means there is no deficit, and no deposit arises under this rule. Where the card names a checking account that the bank's checking records do not hold, there is likewise nothing to restore.

## Input, judgement, output (hypothetical balances)

| Ledger balance of the named checking account | Deficit |
|---|---|
| minus 57.35 USD | 57.35 USD |
| minus 0.62 USD | 0.62 USD |
| 0.00 USD | none |
| 12.40 USD | none |

## Points of judgement

- The figure is the ledger balance itself, not the date on which it went negative; only how far below zero the account stands matters here.
- The ledger balance used is the one on the checking record when the matter is dealt with.
